newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ING gains foothold in U.S. annuities.
newsitem.headline: ING gains foothold in U.S. annuities.

text.p: Dutch financial services group ING Groep NV said its acquisition of life insurer Equitable of Iowa would give it a significant presence in the U.S. market for annuities, an important retirement savings vehicle.
Annuities are contracts that convert the customer's premiums into a stream of payments at regular intervals.
Fixed annuities guarantee a certain level of payments linked to bond yields, while the payout from variable annuities depends on an underlying investment in the stock market.
ING chairman Aad Jacobs said ING's U.S. annuities business had been negligible up to now but that Equitable of Iowa had a two percent share of the overall U.S. annuities market.
Equitable of Iowa ranked sixth in the U.S. in fixed annuities with a 3.5 percent market share and 39th in variable annuities with one percent of the market, he said.
Jacobs told a news conference that both segments offered good growth prospects, with fixed annuities growing at eight to nine percent and variable annuities at 15 percent a year.
Jacobs said that up to now ING had been a little slow to react to the fast growth of the variable annuities market which has been fuelled by the strong stock market.
In addition to complementary products, Jacobs said Equitable of Iowa also brought ING new distribution channels for life insurance products in the U.S.
Equitable of Iowa's products are sold through some 70 regional banks and 400 securities brokers, as well as through the traditional channels of independent and tied sales agents.
Jacobs also noted that Equitable of Iowa operated in 50 U.S. states and Washington D.C.
